edges.text: Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod, take info: ValidationInfo and read earlier fields from info.data instead of values.
Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.

Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.
Replace @root_validator with @model_validator; pre=True becomes mode='before' on a classmethod taking the raw dict, otherwise mode='after' on an instance method returning self.
Replace @root_validator with @model_validator(mode='before') on a classmethod that works on the input dict.

Remove Config.json_encoders; add @field_serializer for the affected fields (or a PlainSerializer in Annotated) that produces the same output, and move other Config keys to model_config = ConfigDict(...).
Remove json_encoders and add a @model_serializer(mode='wrap') that formats datetimes the same way.
Turn the __root__ model into a pydantic.RootModel[...] subclass and use .root instead of .__root__; parse with model_validate.
Replace the __root__ model with a TypeAdapter over the inner type plus a plain helper class.
Replace Model.update_forward_refs() with Model.model_rebuild().

Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod; pre=True becomes mode='before', each_item=True becomes validating the list items in the function, always=True becomes validate_default=True on the Field.
Move the check into an Annotated type with AfterValidator / BeforeValidator.
Replace @validate_arguments with @validate_call.
Rename removed config keys to their v2 names in model_config = ConfigDict(...) (allow_mutation=False->frozen=True, orm_mode->from_attributes, fields={...alias}->Field(alias=...)).
Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod, take info: ValidationInfo and read earlier fields from info.data instead of values.
Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.

Replace `__get_validators__` with a classmethod `__get_pydantic_core_schema__(cls, source_type, handler)` that returns `core_schema.no_info_after_validator_function(cls.validate, core_schema.any_schema())`; import `core_schema` from `pydantic_core`. This preserves `PostCode` as a custom `str` subclass while removing the deprecated hook.

Replace the `PostCode` subclass and its `__get_validators__` hook with a `PostCode = Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(validate_post_code)]` alias. Move the existing normalization and five-digit check into `validate_post_code`, returning the normalized string; import `Annotated` and `BeforeValidator` from `typing` and `pydantic` respectively.
Rename removed config keys to their v2 names in model_config = ConfigDict(...) (allow_mutation=False->frozen=True, orm_mode->from_attributes, fields={...alias}->Field(alias=...)).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model.model_validate(data).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model(**data).
Replace Model.parse_raw(body) with Model.model_validate_json(body).
Replace Model.parse_raw(body) with Model.model_validate(json.loads(body)).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model.model_validate(data).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model(**data).
Replace Model.schema() with Model.model_json_schema().
Replace .copy(update=...) with .model_copy(update=...).
Replace .copy(update=...) with Model(**{**obj.model_dump(), **update}).
Replace Model.__fields__ with Model.model_fields; field.required becomes field.is_required(), outer_type_ becomes annotation.
Set model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True) and replace Model.from_orm(obj) with Model.model_validate(obj).
Replace Model.construct(**data) with Model.model_construct(**data).
Replace .dict(...) with .model_dump(...), keeping the same keyword arguments.
Replace .dict() with dict(obj) and filter keys by hand.
Import Field from pydantic and declare key as `Union[int, str] = Field(union_mode='left_to_right')`. This makes Pydantic try the int branch first, so numeric strings are converted to integers.

Add a `@field_validator('key', mode='before')` that converts string inputs with `int(value)` when conversion succeeds, and otherwise returns the original value. This explicitly turns numeric strings into integers before union validation.
Import ConfigDict and set `model_config = ConfigDict(coerce_numbers_to_str=True)` on `Label`, allowing the integer SKU to validate as the string `"10045"`.
Add a `@field_validator("sku", mode="before")` that converts integer inputs to strings before validation, while leaving other input types unchanged.
Convert the reading at the sensor boundary: pass `units=int(reading)` to `StockLevel` in `from_sensor`, so fractional sensor values are truncated before integer validation.
Add a Pydantic v2 `@field_validator("units", mode="before")` on `StockLevel` that returns `int(value)` for numeric inputs, truncating fractional readings before Pydantic validates the field.
Replace the `parse_obj_as` import and call with `TypeAdapter`: import `TypeAdapter` from `pydantic`, then return `TypeAdapter(List[User]).validate_python(rows)` from `load_users`.
Define a `RootModel` for the user list, such as `class Users(RootModel[list[User]]): pass`, and have `load_users` return `Users.model_validate(rows).root` instead of calling `parse_obj_as`.
Replace .json(...) with .model_dump_json(...), keeping by_alias and other keyword arguments.
Replace .json() with json.dumps(obj.model_dump(mode='json')).

In `changed_fields`, replace `ProfilePatch(**raw).__fields_set__` with `ProfilePatch(**raw).model_fields_set`, then sort the result.

In `changed_fields`, construct the model and return the sorted keys of `model.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`; this preserves explicitly supplied `None` values while avoiding the deprecated `__fields_set__` attribute.

Import field_serializer from pydantic and add a serializer to Quote: @field_serializer("price") def serialize_price(self, value: Decimal) -> float: return float(value). This makes model_dump_json emit price as a JSON number.
Change Quote.price from Decimal to float. Pydantic will then serialize the price as a JSON number, so the decoded value is 12.5 rather than the string "12.50".
Add a Pydantic v2 `@field_serializer("started")` to `Shift` that returns `value.isoformat()`. This serializes UTC datetimes with `+00:00` instead of Pydantic's `Z` form.

Change `to_wire` to build the JSON payload from `s.model_dump(mode="python")`, replacing `started` with `s.started.isoformat()` before calling `json.dumps`. This keeps the wire timestamp in `+00:00` format.

Import `field_serializer` from `pydantic` and add an `@field_serializer("at")` method to `AuditEntry` that returns `value.date().isoformat()`. This keeps `at` as a `datetime` internally while encoding it as `YYYY-MM-DD` in JSON.

Import `model_serializer` from `pydantic` and add a `@model_serializer(mode="wrap")` method to `AuditEntry`. Have it call the handler, replace the serialized `at` value with `self.at.date().isoformat()`, and return the resulting data.
